item.title: main is red: ConvertToCollection reviewed-site census holds a stale duplicate entry for tests/Sniffs.php after the #350/#352 merge

issues.title: main is red: ConvertToCollection reviewed-site census holds a stale duplicate entry for tests/Sniffs.php after the #350/#352 merge
issues.body:
`main` fails CI at HEAD. The failure blocks every open PR, because no branch can reach a green gate while it inherits this.

## The failing test

`tests/Standards/ConvertToCollectionTest.php:541` — `it('reports only the reviewed sites across the package source')`. It compares the sniff's live findings against `CONVERT_TO_COLLECTION_REVIEWED_SITES`, the hand-maintained ledger issue #286 left behind.

Result on `main` HEAD `2664d15`: `1 failed, 2008 passed`. Run [32309976519](https://github.com/mike-bronner/phpcs-rules/actions/runs/32309976519).

## The diagnosis

The ledger records two reviewed sites for `tests/Sniffs.php`. The file holds one.

```
Expected: 'tests/Sniffs.php' => [ ['line' => 204, 'column' => 15], ['line' => 197, 'column' => 15] ]
Found:    'tests/Sniffs.php' => [ ['line' => 205, 'column' => 15] ]
```

There is one native array call in that file, the `array_filter()` in `shippedSmokeSniffs()`. A human reviewed it at `e6f9406`. No new native array call arrived. Only the line number moved.

The duplicate is a merge artifact. Trace the ledger entry across the three merges of 2026-08-19:

| Commit | PR | `tests/Sniffs.php` entry |
|---|---|---|
| `e6f9406` | census regenerated | `[{196, 15}]` |
| `85656ae` | #352 | `[{197, 15}]` |
| `3637e81` | #351 | `[{197, 15}]` |
| `2664d15` | #350 | `[{204, 15}, {197, 15}]` |

PR #350 shifted the same call to line 204 on its own branch and updated its own copy of the ledger. Git merged that edit next to the existing `{197, 15}` line instead of replacing it. Both entries then landed on `main`, and #352's separate additions pushed the real call one line further, to 205.

Each PR passed CI alone. The combination fails. Branch CI runs before the merge, so nothing tested the merged tree.

## The fix

Replace the two entries with the one true site:

```php
'tests/Sniffs.php' => [
    ['line' => 205, 'column' => 15],
],
```

This records a line shift for a call a human already reviewed, and drops a duplicate git created. It blesses no new call site, so it does not weaken the guard.

Verified: apply that edit to a clean `origin/main` worktree and the test passes, `214 assertions`.

## Why this is its own issue

I found this while implementing #334 on PR #355. That PR touches four files, all under `ComponentMarkupSniff`. It touches neither `tests/Sniffs.php` nor any `ConvertToCollection` file. A pristine `origin/main` worktree reproduces the failure with none of PR #355's commits present.

The repair belongs to `main`, not to an unrelated Livewire PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CONVERT_TO_COLLECTION_REVIEWED_SITES` records exactly one site for `tests/Sniffs.php`, at line 205, column 15.
- [ ] `composer test` passes on `main`.
- [ ] The ledger's other entries stay unchanged. Only `tests/Sniffs.php` drifted.
- [ ] Consider a guard against the recurrence: the ledger is a line-number list that two concurrent PRs can each edit and git can merge textually. Record whether a guard is worth adding, or why it is not.

held_acceptance_criteria:
<!-- acceptance-criteria -->

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git diff` (or the PR diff) shows the `'tests/Sniffs.php'` key inside `CONVERT_TO_COLLECTION_REVIEWED_SITES` (in `tests/Standards/ConvertToCollectionTest.php`) appears exactly once as a map key, with its value collapsed to the single tuple `['line' => 205, 'column' => 15]` — not appended alongside the existing `204`/`197` entries, and not achieved by adding a second, later `'tests/Sniffs.php'` key that merely overrides the first at evaluation time.
- [ ] The diff is confined to that one block (the `'tests/Sniffs.php' => [...]` entry, roughly lines 199-202) — no other line in `ConvertToCollectionTest.php` changes, including the `$convertToCollectionSweptFiles` sweep closure and every other file key in the ledger.
- [ ] `composer test` (full, unfiltered — not `--filter`-scoped) is run on a clean checkout of the exact commit being merged (`git status` clean, `git rev-parse HEAD` shown) and the pasted summary line shows the full-suite pass count (`2009 passed`, the issue's `2008 passed` plus the one test this fix turns green) — a restated claim without the transcript does not satisfy this.
- [ ] Before merge, the branch is rebased onto the then-current `main` tip and `composer test` is re-run on that rebased tree, with the `main` SHA it was verified against recorded in the PR. `tests/Sniffs.php` has several other open PRs inserting lines above line 205; a stale rebase can reopen this exact bug within days.
- [ ] The PR names, with `grep` evidence, exactly one call in `tests/Sniffs.php` to a function the `ConvertToCollection` sniff is configured to flag (currently `array_filter()` at line 205) — confirming the corrected entry blesses no new call site and the sniff's configured-function list has no other match in that file. (`array_diff()`/`array_values()` at line 207 are native array calls but outside the sniff's configured scope, not overlooked.)
- [ ] The PR records an explicit decision on a guard against this defect class. The actual defect was two stale/duplicate `line`/`column` tuples surviving a three-way merge inside one file's entry list — not a duplicate top-level key, which PHP itself would silently collapse — and entries drift whenever unrelated lines are inserted above a tracked call site. Either a concrete safeguard addressing that mechanism (e.g., a check that each ledger tuple still resolves to a call of the expected kind at that exact position) is added, or a one-paragraph rationale — naming the mechanism, not boilerplate — explains why none is needed now.
